About the work
We are building an industrial monitoring system to be installed on offshore vessels and rigs. Each installation is a small edge platform: a hypervisor host running Linux service containers and a Windows analytics VM, pulling PLC data into a VM service.
It is deployed and running today (in a lab setup) — but deployment is still manual, the infrastructure-as-code is unproven, and credential handling needs to move to a properly designed rotation model. We have a draft target architecture. We want an experienced engineer to finish it with us, prove it, and make it repeatable across installations.
Installations live on customer vessels. Support is remote, links are constrained, and the people on board are not IT specialists. 

What you'll own:
- Review the target architecture with our team, then finish the IaC and prove it.
- Take us from manual deployment to proven, repeatable Terraform + Ansible — one codebase, per-site config, no hand edits
- Design and build credential rotation protocols. Currently credentials live in a 1Password vault. You will be given a service token with read/write access to vaults.
- Network design and hardening: segmentation, default-deny firewalling, TLS/PKI and trust distribution, secure remote access
- Work directly with vessel and facility IT departments — prepare and defend the network and firewall requests needed to get an installation approved
- Advise us on which industrial cyber security standards and class requirements apply to our installations, identify the gaps, and help assemble what a certification or audit needs
- Write the internal specifications and procedures: architecture specs for our engineers, install and recovery procedures for field techs, security documentation for client IT and auditors

Required
- Experience with zero trust networks e.g: Twingate
- Strong hands-on networking: routing, VLANs, segmentation, firewalling, DNS/NTP — and the habit of verifying reachability rather than trusting configuration
- Production Terraform and Ansible; Debian-family Linux; Proxmox VE ; containers
- Familiarity with industrial/OT security standards (IEC 62443 and related), and the judgment to say what applies to a given installation
- Clear written English and the confidence to represent us on a technical call with a client's IT department
- Comfortable holding production credentials under NDA

Nice to have:
- Marine, offshore or rig experience; class society cyber requirements
- MQTT or other industrial protocols; PostgreSQL operations; CI/CD; Windows in a mixed fleet

similarJobs.title: Automotive HUD / Optical Systems Engineer — Low-Profile Daylight Windshield HUD Feasibility
similarJobs.description:
I’m looking for an experienced automotive HUD / optical systems engineer for a paid consultation and feasibility assessment on an early-stage vehicle heads-up display product.

The goal is NOT to optimize an existing monitor, pico projector, enclosure, or temporary prototype setup.

I am trying to determine the most practical optical and hardware architecture for a future standalone vehicle HUD unit, with particular emphasis on achieving a LOW-PROFILE dash-mounted package while maintaining excellent daylight readability.

The desired product is a compact, self-contained device mounted on top of the vehicle dashboard that projects a simple text-based virtual image into the driver’s forward field of view.

A major design goal is for the physical hardware to be unobtrusive enough that the driver largely stops noticing the device itself while driving.


KEY PACKAGING REQUIREMENT

Vertical height is the primary packaging constraint.

The preferred finished enclosure target is approximately:

- 2.0–2.5 inches tall
- approximately 51–64 mm

A slightly wider or deeper enclosure is acceptable if it allows the system to become substantially lower-profile.

This height target applies to the COMPLETE practical assembly, not just the light engine. The engineer should consider:

- projection/display engine
- required heatsink and cooling
- optical components
- mirrors / magnification optics
- electronics
- mechanical clearances
- enclosure walls
- adjustment mechanisms
- airflow

I am specifically interested in determining whether this height range is technically realistic.

If it is not, I want an evidence-based explanation of the minimum practical height and which requirement creates the limitation.

No enclosure CAD or physical prototype should be developed until the optical architecture and approximate component stack-up support a credible package size.


DISPLAY REQUIREMENTS

The actual display content is extremely simple.

The HUD only needs to present approximately four rows of large, high-contrast text.

Because of this, very high display resolution is not automatically required. Brightness, contrast, optical efficiency, image stability, viewing position, and readability are more important than producing a high-resolution video image.

This consultation is focused on HUD hardware and optics, not software development.


DAYLIGHT READABILITY

Daylight performance is a HARD requirement.

The display must remain clearly readable in very bright outdoor conditions, including harsh Texas sunlight and situations where strong sunlight is entering or striking the windshield.

All displayed text fields should remain usable rather than washing out.

I am not interested in a solution that works well indoors, at dusk, or only in moderate lighting but becomes difficult to read in direct daytime conditions.

The engineer should evaluate actual HUD/image luminance and optical efficiency rather than relying solely on a projector’s advertised lumen rating.

The same system must also be capable of dimming sufficiently for nighttime use.


DESIRED SYSTEM CHARACTERISTICS

The system should ideally:

- project a virtual image through the vehicle windshield
- produce a clear image in the driver’s normal forward field of view
- remain readable in harsh daylight as well as at night
- minimize windshield ghosting / double images
- support practical image-position adjustment for drivers of different heights and seating positions
- provide a usable eyebox rather than requiring the driver’s head to remain in one exact location
- avoid requiring a custom windshield if reasonably possible
- avoid windshield film if reasonably possible
- avoid a permanent external/pop-up combiner plate if reasonably possible
- operate from normal vehicle power
- tolerate vehicle vibration and temperature conditions
- be practical for installation in public-safety vehicles
- use a secure, preferably no-drill mounting approach
- eventually be manufacturable in quantity


IMPORTANT: OPTICAL ARCHITECTURE IS OPEN

I do NOT want the engineer to assume that a conventional large Fresnel lens, simple fold mirror, or existing prototype optical layout must be retained.

The optical architecture is still open.

I am specifically interested in determining whether other approaches could provide a substantially thinner package, including where appropriate:

- automotive-style folded HUD optics
- freeform reflective optics
- aspheric mirrors
- off-axis magnification
- compact picture-generation units (PGUs)
- multiple-fold optical paths
- reflective magnification
- alternative pupil-forming approaches
- compact DLP or other suitable light engines
- architectures that trade additional width/depth for reduced height

A smaller projector alone is not considered sufficient if the magnification and relay optics still require a tall enclosure.


AREAS I WOULD LIKE HELP EVALUATING

- practical windshield HUD architectures for a dash-top product
- whether approximately 51–64 mm finished height is achievable
- windshield projection versus integrated combiner approaches
- alternative optical layouts capable of reducing vertical packaging height
- suitable projection/display-engine technologies
- automotive HUD picture-generation units
- required daytime luminance / brightness
- optical efficiency and expected light losses
- contrast requirements
- virtual-image distance / focal distance
- field of view
- required optical aperture
- eyebox and driver viewing-position requirements
- image size and positioning
- windshield angle and curvature
- laminated-windshield considerations
- ghosting / double reflections
- ways to reduce ghosting without immediately requiring windshield film or custom glass
- different driver heights and seat positions
- adjustment methods that do not require physically repositioning the entire unit
- thermal management
- parked-vehicle temperature considerations
- vibration
- automotive electrical power
- suitable light-engine technologies
- off-the-shelf optical modules or PGUs that could support an early prototype
- practical packaging for a compact standalone unit
- component availability in prototype quantities
- preliminary BOM / expected prototype cost
- manufacturing path and major cost drivers at higher quantities
- which technologies are appropriate for an early prototype versus eventual production
- technical risks that should be proven before significant money is spent


CURRENT PROJECT STATUS

I have already performed basic physical fit testing with an early enclosure mockup.

That testing confirmed that a roughly 4-inch / 100+ mm tall dash-mounted enclosure is too bulky for the intended application.

This is why low-profile optical packaging is now a major requirement.

I also have some off-the-shelf HUD/display components and preliminary optical work available for discussion under NDA.

However, those components and layouts are NOT intended to constrain the final architecture.

No specific projector or light engine should be assumed to be permanently selected.


INITIAL SCOPE

The initial engagement is intentionally focused on optical feasibility and architecture before additional hardware is purchased or another enclosure is fabricated.

I anticipate approximately a 60–90 minute video consultation, review of the product requirements and relevant existing work, followed by a detailed written engineering assessment.

If meaningful ray tracing, optical modeling, or additional analysis is required beyond the initial consultation, I am open to discussing a clearly defined additional milestone before proceeding.


INITIAL DELIVERABLE

The written engineering assessment should ideally include:

- recommended HUD optical architecture
- assessment of whether a 51–64 mm finished enclosure height is technically realistic
- minimum practical height if 51–64 mm is not realistic
- explanation of the optical constraints controlling minimum height
- windshield versus combiner recommendation
- recommended approach to reducing vertical optical stack height
- recommended projection/display technology
- recommended light-engine or PGU candidates
- brightness / luminance targets for harsh daylight
- expected optical efficiency and major light losses
- resolution actually required for four rows of large text
- field of view recommendation
- virtual-image-distance recommendation
- eyebox requirements
- windshield ghosting / double-image analysis
- methods for reducing ghosting
- driver-position adjustment approach
- preliminary optical stack-up / side-profile concept
- approximate COMPLETE system dimensions
- thermal and cooling considerations
- recommended physical architecture for a standalone dash-top unit
- recommended components or component classes for an early prototype
- rough 3–10 unit pilot BOM and cost range
- prototype versus eventual production architecture considerations
- expected technical risks
- recommended experiments and validation tests
- hardware approaches or purchases that should be avoided
- clear go/no-go questions that should be answered before enclosure CAD or fabrication
- next steps toward a pilot-ready standalone HUD


IMPORTANT DEVELOPMENT APPROACH

I am intentionally trying to avoid purchasing hardware or fabricating multiple enclosures based on unproven assumptions.

The preferred sequence is:

1. Establish credible optical architecture.
2. Determine real component dimensions.
3. Include cooling and electronics.
4. Model the complete optical/mechanical stack.
5. Establish a defensible finished enclosure envelope.
6. Only then proceed to detailed enclosure CAD and physical fabrication.

I am looking for an engineer who is comfortable identifying when a requirement is difficult or unrealistic rather than simply designing around whatever components are initially available.


IDEAL EXPERIENCE

I am specifically looking for someone with real professional experience in one or more of the following:

- automotive heads-up displays
- OEM or aftermarket windshield HUD systems
- optical system design
- automotive picture-generation units / PGUs
- freeform or aspheric reflective optics
- folded optical systems
- virtual-image systems
- combiners / reflective optics
- projection systems
- aircraft HUDs
- helmet-mounted displays
- automotive display integration
- optical ray tracing / modeling
- optical prototyping
- low-volume automotive hardware development


WHEN APPLYING

Please describe any relevant work you have completed involving:

- automotive HUD systems
- windshield projection
- automotive PGUs
- freeform or aspheric optics
- folded optical systems
- virtual-image displays
- aircraft HUDs
- helmet-mounted displays
- optical combiners
- compact projection systems
- automotive display development

Please also identify which optical design/modeling tools you normally use, such as Zemax OpticStudio, Code V, LightTools, TracePro, or equivalent tools.

If possible, briefly explain whether you have previously worked on systems where optical packaging height, eyebox, field of view, and daylight luminance had to be optimized together.

Generic consumer-projector or enclosure-design experience alone is not what I am looking for.


POTENTIAL FUTURE WORK

This initial engagement is intentionally limited to consultation, feasibility, and technical direction.

However, if the consultation is a good fit and the project reaches its next development milestones, there may be opportunities for additional paid engineering work.

Possible future phases could include:

- optical architecture development and refinement
- ray tracing and tolerance analysis
- prototype HUD optical design
- component selection and sourcing
- optical testing and validation
- enclosure / packaging development
- automotive power and thermal integration
- pilot-unit engineering
- design-for-manufacturing work
- support during a small public-safety vehicle pilot
- later production-hardware development

There is no guarantee of future work, and this is not currently a full-time or contract-to-hire position.

The goal is to find an experienced engineer who could potentially continue working with the project if there is a strong technical and working relationship.


CONFIDENTIALITY

This is an unreleased early-stage product.

The public job description intentionally does not include proprietary software, algorithms, detailed system architecture, or unique implementation details.

The selected consultant must be willing to sign a confidentiality/NDA agreement before receiving detailed non-public product information or proprietary materials.


OVERALL GOAL

The immediate goal is to determine whether a genuinely low-profile, daylight-readable, standalone automotive HUD can be built for this application before significant money is committed to hardware, custom optics, enclosure fabrication, or tooling.

I am looking for engineering evidence first, hardware second.

WordPress Developer (Freelance / Retainer)

Company: RankFast Digital

Location: Remote (India), overlap with IST working hours

Engagement: Monthly retainer, approx. 60 to 90 hours per month across 6 to 8 client websites. Can convert to full time if workload grows.

Reports to: Growth/Account Operator handling the relevant client

About the role
RankFast is a digital marketing agency serving clients in the US, UK, Canada, UAE and Australia. Our clients run on WordPress and we need a developer who can take a change request from a client call and ship it the same week without hand holding. You will be the only dev seat, working alongside SEO and paid media operators who define what needs to change and why. You own how.

This is execution work on live client sites, not greenfield product development. Speed, reliability and clean handovers matter more than framework depth.

What you will actually do: 

Everything below comes from our real workload over the last quarter:
Page builds and edits
Build and edit pages in Elementor: landing pages, service pages, retreat/program pages, video library pages

Header, footer and global template changes across sites

Popups, banners and section-level redesigns from client feedback

Embed and organise video content (YouTube integrations, video sections on blog pages)

Forms, bookings and automations
Build and test contact and booking forms, add fields, verify email delivery

Calendly and booking tool configuration and troubleshooting

Connect lead sources to email lists and CRMs (e.g. Meta lead forms to email via Make/Zapier or native integrations)

Fixes and maintenance
Debug plugin conflicts (duplicate page issues, broken elements after content removal)

Resolve site-level issues: redirects, www/non-www resolution, DNS and SSL basics, 404s

Page speed and Core Web Vitals improvements

Pre-launch and post-launch QA on redesigned sites: test forms, links, mobile rendering

SEO implementation (you implement, the SEO team specifies)
Fix technical issues flagged in Google Search Console and Semrush audits: invalid structured data, sitemap errors, broken internal links, missing anchor text, meta title/description updates in bulk

opening.description:
Senior Full-Stack Developer / Product Engineer Needed to Complete and Perfect Existing Marketplace Website Within 7 Days

I am looking for an experienced senior full-stack developer or product engineer who can manage the technical development of an existing website from end to end and bring it to a polished, fully functioning, launch-ready standard.

Website: titlesales.com.au

The website has already been substantially built and is currently very close to the Figma design. This is not a complete rebuild or redesign.

The existing live website and Figma design are near identical, with relatively small changes, corrections, missing elements and refinements required throughout. There are also areas of functionality that need to be checked, completed and thoroughly tested.

This is a priority project. We want the website completed, perfected, fully tested and ready to publish within 7 days of commencement.

You must have sufficient availability to prioritise this project during that period.

Current setup

The platform currently uses:

* Figma for design
* Claude Code for development assistance
* GitHub for the codebase
* Supabase for database, authentication and backend functionality
* Vercel for hosting and deployment
* Stripe for payments
* Other integrations and services as required

I currently have a designer working on the Figma designs and have been using Claude Code to implement those designs.

The difficulty is that I am spending too much time going backwards and forwards between the designer, Figma, Claude Code and the live website.

I need someone who can step in, understand the existing platform, compare it against Figma, identify what needs to be corrected or completed and take care of the technical implementation without requiring every individual issue to be pointed out.

The website and Figma are already very close

It is important to understand that most of the website has already been built.

The Figma design is near identical to the existing live website, with mainly small changes and refinements required throughout.

We are not looking for somebody to redesign or rebuild the entire platform.

The work is primarily about:

* Perfecting the existing implementation
* Completing anything that is missing
* Correcting inconsistencies
* Fixing functionality
* Ensuring all pages connect correctly
* Ensuring mobile and desktop versions are complete
* Implementing remaining Figma changes
* Testing every feature and user journey
* Completing final polish before launch

You can view the existing website before submitting your proposal:

titlesales.com.au

Attention to detail is an absolute must

This is one of the most important requirements of the role.

We expect an extremely high standard and we expect perfection in the final result.

We are not looking for somebody who considers something complete because it is approximately correct or “close enough”.

The finished website needs to accurately reflect the Figma design, including:

* Spacing
* Alignment
* Typography
* Font sizes and weights
* Button sizes and positioning
* Border radiuses
* Component sizing
* Icons
* Colours
* Responsive behaviour
* Mobile layouts
* Consistency between pages
* Hover, active and selected states
* Loading states
* Empty states
* Error states
* Navigation
* Forms
* Validation
* User flows
* Overall visual polish

If something is slightly misaligned, inconsistent, missing, visually incorrect or functioning differently from what was intended, we expect you to notice it and correct it.

We do not want to have to identify every small issue ourselves.

The successful developer should naturally check their own work carefully across different pages, devices and screen sizes before considering something complete.

“Close enough” is not the standard we are looking for.

Initiative is extremely important

I am also looking for somebody who will actively think about the product rather than simply complete a list of tasks.

If you see something that could be improved, simplified, made more intuitive, made more professional or made easier for users, I want you to raise it.

I want someone who will look at the website as a whole and think:

* Is there a better way to do this?
* Is anything missing?
* Is this user journey confusing?
* Could this page be clearer?
* Could this process require fewer steps?
* Is there functionality users would reasonably expect that is not currently there?
* Could the mobile experience be improved?
* Could performance be improved?
* Are there inconsistencies we have not noticed?
* Is there a better technical approach?
* Is there anything that would make the platform feel more polished, trustworthy or professional?

I value developers who make thoughtful suggestions and identify opportunities without waiting to be asked.

You do not need to blindly follow the existing implementation if you can see a genuinely better solution.

At the same time, significant design, functionality or structural changes should be discussed with us before being implemented.

The ideal person will be able to distinguish between something that should simply be fixed and something that could genuinely be improved.

What I need

I need one highly capable developer who can manage the technical implementation of the website and work through it systematically.

I want to be able to provide access to the Figma designs, GitHub repository and relevant platforms and have you handle the technical side of bringing everything together properly.

This will include:

* Reviewing and understanding the existing codebase
* Comparing the live website directly against Figma
* Implementing remaining Figma changes accurately
* Ensuring the website matches Figma across desktop and mobile
* Creating any missing pages or components
* Updating existing pages
* Connecting buttons, links, menus and navigation correctly
* Making sure all user journeys function correctly
* Managing Supabase database functionality
* Managing authentication and permissions
* Managing Stripe payments and related functionality
* Managing GitHub and version control
* Managing Vercel deployments
* Fixing existing bugs and inconsistencies
* Ensuring changes do not break existing functionality
* Testing changes properly before deployment
* Identifying missing pages, features or connections
* Communicating directly with the designer where necessary
* Helping determine the best technical implementation for new features
* Suggesting improvements where you believe the product can be made better
* Identifying functionality or UX improvements we may have overlooked
* Completing final QA
* Preparing the platform for launch

I do not want to micromanage every change

I am not looking for somebody who needs every individual task explained step by step.

I do not want to constantly have to say:

“Move this button.”

“Fix this spacing.”

“Connect this page.”

“Create the mobile version.”

“This button should go here.”

“This feature isn’t working.”

I need somebody experienced enough to look at the Figma file, compare it with the live website and existing codebase, understand what is intended and implement it correctly.

If there is a page or feature in Figma, I expect you to be able to determine:

* Where it belongs
* How it should function
* What it needs to connect to
* Whether database changes are required
* Whether authentication or permissions are involved
* How it should work on mobile
* Whether it affects other pages or workflows
* What needs to be tested before it goes live
* Whether there is an obvious opportunity to make it better

The goal is to significantly reduce the amount of technical coordination required from me.

About Title Sales

Title Sales is an Australian property marketplace connecting property owners directly with buyers.

The platform includes functionality such as:

* Property listings
* Seller accounts
* Buyer accounts
* Buyer requirements and briefs
* Listing management
* Search and filtering
* Messaging
* Notifications
* Payments
* Listing packages
* User dashboards
* Administration functionality
* Responsive mobile layouts
* Various marketplace features

A significant amount of development has already been completed.

Again, this is not a project starting from scratch.

Confidentiality and NDA

This project is commercially sensitive.

The successful applicant will be required to sign an NDA and confidentiality agreement before being provided with full access to the project, codebase, Figma files, systems, business information or other confidential material.

All project information, designs, code, data, concepts, workflows, business information, documentation and access credentials must be treated as strictly confidential.

Project material must not be:

* Shared with any third party
* Published
* Used in a portfolio without written permission
* Reused for another client
* Uploaded to public repositories
* Distributed to subcontractors without prior approval
* Discussed publicly

We expect professional handling of all credentials, source code, database access and confidential information.

7-day timeframe

Our immediate objective is to have the website:

* Reviewed
* Corrected
* Completed
* Tested
* Fully responsive
* Functioning properly
* Visually perfected
* Ready to publish

within 7 days of commencing the project.

This project needs to be prioritised.

Please only apply if you have genuine availability over the next 7 days and can dedicate enough time to completing the project properly.

There may be ongoing development work after launch for the right person.

Skills required

Strong experience is required with:

* Full-stack web development
* Modern front-end development
* Supabase
* PostgreSQL
* Authentication and user permissions
* GitHub
* Vercel
* Stripe
* Responsive web development
* Figma implementation
* API integrations
* Debugging existing applications
* Existing codebases
* QA and cross-device testing
* Pixel-accurate implementation
* Production deployment
* UX thinking and product improvement

Experience with React, Next.js and TypeScript is also highly regarded, depending on the existing stack.

Experience with marketplaces, SaaS platforms or applications involving multiple user types would be ideal.

Experience with AI-assisted development tools such as Claude Code is useful, but you must understand the underlying code and be capable of independently reviewing, debugging and improving it.

When submitting your proposal

Please review titlesales.com.au before submitting your proposal so you understand the current state of the website.

Please include:

* Examples of complex websites or applications you have personally worked on
* Examples where you have taken over an existing partially completed codebase
* Your experience with Supabase, Vercel, GitHub and Stripe
* Your experience implementing Figma designs
* Whether you personally handle both front-end and back-end development
* Your experience with responsive/mobile implementation
* How you ensure your implementation accurately matches Figma
* How you test your work before considering it complete
* An example of a project where you identified and suggested improvements beyond what the client originally requested
* Your availability over the next 7 days
* How many hours you can realistically dedicate during that period
* Confirmation that you are comfortable signing an NDA and confidentiality agreement

Please submit your very best price

Because the website is already substantially built and the Figma design is near identical to the current implementation, please submit your very best and most competitive price for completing the project.

We are looking at both capability and value.

Please review the existing website before quoting rather than assuming this is a complete website build from scratch.

We want applicants to provide their best realistic price upfront based on completing, correcting, testing and perfecting the existing platform.

Please do not submit an inflated placeholder quote with the intention of substantially increasing it immediately afterwards.

If there are specific items you believe cannot reasonably be priced until you have reviewed the codebase, please clearly identify those in your proposal.

Final requirement

Please do not send a generic proposal.

We are looking for someone experienced, highly organised, responsive, proactive and extremely particular about their work.

We want someone who will not only complete what is asked, but will also identify opportunities to make Title Sales better.

Attention to detail is an absolute must.

Initiative is essential.

The project must be prioritised.

The target is to have Title Sales perfected, tested and ready to publish within 7 days.

Please review titlesales.com.au and submit your very best price.

job_title: Senior Full-Stack Developer / Product Engineer Needed to Complete and Perfect Existing Marketplace
job_detail:
Senior Full-Stack Developer / Product Engineer Needed to Complete and Perfect Existing Marketplace Website Within 7 Days

I am looking for an experienced senior full-stack developer or product engineer who can manage the technical development of an existing website from end to end and bring it to a polished, fully functioning, launch-ready standard.

Website: titlesales.com.au

The website has already been substantially built and is currently very close to the Figma design. This is not a complete rebuild or redesign.

The existing live website and Figma design are near identical, with relatively small changes, corrections, missing elements and refinements required throughout. There are also areas of functionality that need to be checked, completed and thoroughly tested.

This is a priority project. We want the website completed, perfected, fully tested and ready to publish within 7 days of commencement.

You must have sufficient availability to prioritise this project during that period.

Current setup

The platform currently uses:

* Figma for design
* Claude Code for development assistance
* GitHub for the codebase
* Supabase for database, authentication and backend functionality
* Vercel for hosting and deployment
* Stripe for payments
* Other integrations and services as required

I currently have a designer working on the Figma designs and have been using Claude Code to implement those designs.

The difficulty is that I am spending too much time going backwards and forwards between the designer, Figma, Claude Code and the live website.

I need someone who can step in, understand the existing platform, compare it against Figma, identify what needs to be corrected or completed and take care of the technical implementation without requiring every individual issue to be pointed out.

The website and Figma are already very close

It is important to understand that most of the website has already been built.

The Figma design is near identical to the existing live website, with mainly small changes and refinements required throughout.

We are not looking for somebody to redesign or rebuild the entire platform.

The work is primarily about:

* Perfecting the existing implementation
* Completing anything that is missing
* Correcting inconsistencies
* Fixing functionality
* Ensuring all pages connect correctly
* Ensuring mobile and desktop versions are complete
* Implementing remaining Figma changes
* Testing every feature and user journey
* Completing final polish before launch

You can view the existing website before submitting your proposal:

titlesales.com.au

Attention to detail is an absolute must

This is one of the most important requirements of the role.

We expect an extremely high standard and we expect perfection in the final result.

We are not looking for somebody who considers something complete because it is approximately correct or “close enough”.

The finished website needs to accurately reflect the Figma design, including:

* Spacing
* Alignment
* Typography
* Font sizes and weights
* Button sizes and positioning
* Border radiuses
* Component sizing
* Icons
* Colours
* Responsive behaviour
* Mobile layouts
* Consistency between pages
* Hover, active and selected states
* Loading states
* Empty states
* Error states
* Navigation
* Forms
* Validation
* User flows
* Overall visual polish

If something is slightly misaligned, inconsistent, missing, visually incorrect or functioning differently from what was intended, we expect you to notice it and correct it.

We do not want to have to identify every small issue ourselves.

The successful developer should naturally check their own work carefully across different pages, devices and screen sizes before considering something complete.

“Close enough” is not the standard we are looking for.

Initiative is extremely important

I am also looking for somebody who will actively think about the product rather than simply complete a list of tasks.

If you see something that could be improved, simplified, made more intuitive, made more professional or made easier for users, I want you to raise it.

I want someone who will look at the website as a whole and think:

* Is there a better way to do this?
* Is anything missing?
* Is this user journey confusing?
* Could this page be clearer?
* Could this process require fewer steps?
* Is there functionality users would reasonably expect that is not currently there?
* Could the mobile experience be improved?
* Could performance be improved?
* Are there inconsistencies we have not noticed?
* Is there a better technical approach?
* Is there anything that would make the platform feel more polished, trustworthy or professional?

I value developers who make thoughtful suggestions and identify opportunities without waiting to be asked.

You do not need to blindly follow the existing implementation if you can see a genuinely better solution.

At the same time, significant design, functionality or structural changes should be discussed with us before being implemented.

The ideal person will be able to distinguish between something that should simply be fixed and something that could genuinely be improved.

What I need

I need one highly capable developer who can manage the technical implementation of the website and work through it systematically.

I want to be able to provide access to the Figma designs, GitHub repository and relevant platforms and have you handle the technical side of bringing everything together properly.

This will include:

* Reviewing and understanding the existing codebase
* Comparing the live website directly against Figma
* Implementing remaining Figma changes accurately
* Ensuring the website matches Figma across desktop and mobile
* Creating any missing pages or components
* Updating existing pages
* Connecting buttons, links, menus and navigation correctly
* Making sure all user journeys function correctly
* Managing Supabase database functionality
* Managing authentication and permissions
* Managing Stripe payments and related functionality
* Managing GitHub and version control
* Managing Vercel deployments
* Fixing existing bugs and inconsistencies
* Ensuring changes do not break existing functionality
* Testing changes properly before deployment
* Identifying missing pages, features or connections
* Communicating directly with the designer where necessary
* Helping determine the best technical implementation for new features
* Suggesting improvements where you believe the product can be made better
* Identifying functionality or UX improvements we may have overlooked
* Completing final QA
* Preparing the platform for launch

I do not want to micromanage every change

I am not looking for somebody who needs every individual task explained step by step.

I do not want to constantly have to say:

“Move this button.”

“Fix this spacing.”

“Connect this page.”

“Create the mobile version.”

“This button should go here.”

“This feature isn’t working.”

I need somebody experienced enough to look at the Figma file, compare it with the live website and existing codebase, understand what is intended and implement it correctly.

If there is a page or feature in Figma, I expect you to be able to determine:

* Where it belongs
* How it should function
* What it needs to connect to
* Whether database changes are required
* Whether authentication or permissions are involved
* How it should work on mobile
* Whether it affects other pages or workflows
* What needs to be tested before it goes live
* Whether there is an obvious opportunity to make it better

The goal is to significantly reduce the amount of technical coordination required from me.

About Title Sales

Title Sales is an Australian property marketplace connecting property owners directly with buyers.

The platform includes functionality such as:

* Property listings
* Seller accounts
* Buyer accounts
* Buyer requirements and briefs
* Listing management
* Search and filtering
* Messaging
* Notifications
* Payments
* Listing packages
* User dashboards
* Administration functionality
* Responsive mobile layouts
* Various marketplace features

A significant amount of development has already been completed.

Again, this is not a project starting from scratch.

Confidentiality and NDA

This project is commercially sensitive.

The successful applicant will be required to sign an NDA and confidentiality agreement before being provided with full access to the project, codebase, Figma files, systems, business information or other confidential material.

All project information, designs, code, data, concepts, workflows, business information, documentation and access credentials must be treated as strictly confidential.

Project material must not be:

* Shared with any third party
* Published
* Used in a portfolio without written permission
* Reused for another client
* Uploaded to public repositories
* Distributed to subcontractors without prior approval
* Discussed publicly

We expect professional handling of all credentials, source code, database access and confidential information.

7-day timeframe

Our immediate objective is to have the website:

* Reviewed
* Corrected
* Completed
* Tested
* Fully responsive
* Functioning properly
* Visually perfected
* Ready to publish

within 7 days of commencing the project.

This project needs to be prioritised.

Please only apply if you have genuine availability over the next 7 days and can dedicate enough time to completing the project properly.

There may be ongoing development work after launch for the right person.

Skills required

Strong experience is required with:

* Full-stack web development
* Modern front-end development
* Supabase
* PostgreSQL
* Authentication and user permissions
* GitHub
* Vercel
* Stripe
* Responsive web development
* Figma implementation
* API integrations
* Debugging existing applications
* Existing codebases
* QA and cross-device testing
* Pixel-accurate implementation
* Production deployment
* UX thinking and product improvement

Experience with React, Next.js and TypeScript is also highly regarded, depending on the existing stack.

Experience with marketplaces, SaaS platforms or applications involving multiple user types would be ideal.

Experience with AI-assisted development tools such as Claude Code is useful, but you must understand the underlying code and be capable of independently reviewing, debugging and improving it.

When submitting your proposal

Please review titlesales.com.au before submitting your proposal so you understand the current state of the website.

Please include:

* Examples of complex websites or applications you have personally worked on
* Examples where you have taken over an existing partially completed codebase
* Your experience with Supabase, Vercel, GitHub and Stripe
* Your experience implementing Figma designs
* Whether you personally handle both front-end and back-end development
* Your experience with responsive/mobile implementation
* How you ensure your implementation accurately matches Figma
* How you test your work before considering it complete
* An example of a project where you identified and suggested improvements beyond what the client originally requested
* Your availability over the next 7 days
* How many hours you can realistically dedicate during that period
* Confirmation that you are comfortable signing an NDA and confidentiality agreement

Please submit your very best price

Because the website is already substantially built and the Figma design is near identical to the current implementation, please submit your very best and most competitive price for completing the project.

We are looking at both capability and value.

Please review the existing website before quoting rather than assuming this is a complete website build from scratch.

We want applicants to provide their best realistic price upfront based on completing, correcting, testing and perfecting the existing platform.

Please do not submit an inflated placeholder quote with the intention of substantially increasing it immediately afterwards.

If there are specific items you believe cannot reasonably be priced until you have reviewed the codebase, please clearly identify those in your proposal.

Final requirement

Please do not send a generic proposal.

We are looking for someone experienced, highly organised, responsive, proactive and extremely particular about their work.

We want someone who will not only complete what is asked, but will also identify opportunities to make Title Sales better.

Attention to detail is an absolute must.

Initiative is essential.

The project must be prioritised.

The target is to have Title Sales perfected, tested and ready to publish within 7 days.

Please review titlesales.com.au and submit your very best price.

title: Automation for Personalized Card Generation

opening.description:
Automate my personalized affirmation card workflow (Typeform → Claude API → card design, incl. astrology)

I create personalized affirmation card sets. Right now most of the process is manual, and I'm looking for someone to automate it end to end so I can produce sets faster and more reliably.

Current workflow

- A customer fills out a Typeform. If she chooses astrology, I calculate her chart manually on astro.com. Then I run her answers (plus the chart data) through Claude with my prompt and format the output into a 2-column CSV. Finally, I upload the CSV to Canva and use Bulk Create to generate the cards.

Scope of work

- Connect Typeform submissions to the Claude API using my existing prompt
- Astrology option (required): Customers choose in the Typeform whether their cards include astrology. If they opt in, they provide birth date, time and place. The workflow should then calculate the chart automatically and pass it into the prompt. Cards without astrology use the standard prompt. Results need to match astro.com, so Swiss Ephemeris (the engine behind astro.com) or an API built on it would be ideal.
- Convert the Claude output into a clean, structured 2-column CSV (or a direct data feed)
- Automatically generate the card designs from a template (currently Canva Bulk Create)
- Recommend and set up the automation tool that fits best (e.g. Make, Zapier, n8n)
- Include a review step so I can approve the texts before cards are generated
Document the setup so I can maintain it myself, and do a test run with sample data (with and without astrology)

Open to alternatives to Canva

As far as I know, Canva's Bulk Create can't be triggered automatically without an Enterprise plan. If you know a better tool for generating designs from templates via API (e.g. Placid, Bannerbear, Templated.io, Google Slides), I'd love your recommendation. The cards need to look high-quality and stay easy for me to edit.

In your proposal, please tell me

- Which tool stack you would use, and the estimated monthly running costs (including any licensing for the astrology calculation)
- Whether you've worked with the Claude or OpenAI API before
- Your recommendation for the design step (Canva or an alternative), and why
Your estimated timeline

I'm a Senior Product Designer with an existing Framer portfolio and several detailed case studies based on genuine professional work.
The work itself is strong, but the portfolio has become too long and detailed. I want to transform it into a much more concise, highly scannable and compelling portfolio for Senior Product Design roles.

This is not a portfolio review or coaching engagement.
I'm looking for someone who can take ownership of the transformation and do the hands-on work.
I already have the projects, evidence, designs and detailed case-study content. I need an experienced specialist to decide what to keep, cut and prioritise; restructure and rewrite the content; strengthen the storytelling and hierarchy; and redesign the portfolio so that the strongest evidence is immediately clear to recruiters and hiring managers.
The key challenge is making the work significantly shorter and easier to scan without losing the complexity, judgement and senior-level thinking behind it.

WRITING AND STORYTELLING
Writing quality is particularly important.
My work involves complex products, services, systems, research and strategic design decisions. I need someone who can understand that material and turn it into clear, concise, natural English while retaining its specificity and credibility.
I don't want generic UX language, textbook-process storytelling, invented metrics or fabricated research simply to make a case study look complete.
I want the final portfolio to make my individual contribution, important decisions, constraints, trade-offs, influence and outcomes easy to understand.

VISUAL DIRECTION
I'm looking for something restrained, sophisticated and editorial.
Strong typography, hierarchy, spacing and thoughtful visual storytelling matter more to me than effects or elaborate interaction. Subtle motion is fine where it genuinely improves the experience, but I'm not looking for an animation-heavy or gimmicky portfolio.
The existing site is built in Framer. Framer experience would be a strong advantage and I would ideally like the final work implemented there, but it is not essential if you are an exceptional fit for the portfolio strategy, writing and design work.

THE RIGHT PERSON WILL IDEALLY HAVE
- Senior Product Design / UX experience and/or specialist experience creating Product Design portfolios
- Strong understanding of how senior Product Designers are evaluated during hiring
- Excellent written English and strong editorial judgement
- Demonstrable Product/UX case-study storytelling experience
- Strong visual design and information-hierarchy skills
- The confidence to make decisions independently rather than relying on me to art-direct the work

Experience hiring or reviewing Product Designers would be particularly valuable.
I'm much more interested in relevant Product Design portfolio expertise than generic website design, graphic design or marketing case-study experience.

SCOPE
I would expect the project to involve reviewing the portfolio as a whole, establishing the right positioning and hierarchy, fully transforming the priority case studies, refining the homepage where needed, and producing a cohesive final portfolio.
I would like to start by completing one case study so we can establish the approach before applying it across the rest of the portfolio.
I'm open to your recommendation on the best project structure and deliverables based on what you see in the existing work.

WHEN APPLYING
Please share the most relevant Product Design / UX portfolio or case-study work that you personally contributed to, particularly examples where you were responsible for both storytelling/content and visual design.
Please be clear about which parts you personally handled.
I'm specifically looking for someone who can take this on as a hands-on, end-to-end engagement rather than an advisory session.

All source materials and portfolio content shared during the project should be treated as confidential and should not be published or reused without explicit permission.
